report:
Summary conclusion
- There is a clear, interpretable difference: it’s concentrated on the residual at the first token (position 0) across many middle-to-late layers, and it pushes logits toward vocabulary associated with newsy/incident/medical/legal/tragedy-style words and some instruction-like tokens. In short: model B (B − A) applies an initial-token bias that steers early continuations toward a “news/incident/tragic/clinic/law” register compared with A.

Why I conclude this
- Spatial pattern: the L2-norm is overwhelmingly largest at position 0 across many layers (layers ~4–25), with much smaller values at p1–p4. That means the difference mainly affects the first-token residual stream (i.e., how the model starts a fresh prompt / the initial next-token logits).
- Logit-lens evidence: the top tokens that the difference vectors point toward include a coherent cluster of event/negative/medical/legal words in mid-to-late layers: e.g. tragic, tragedy, law, surgeon, clinic, downturn, rescue, heard, heard/curse/doom variants, Royals/Manny (news/sports names), coming/blitz/shocked, and other reporting-style words. Earlier layers show some other nouns (bottle, wings, Author) but the strongest signal in later layers consistently favors words that appear in news or incident reports.
- Together this points to a shift in the prior over early continuations: B tends to bias the model’s start-of-sequence logits toward vocabulary that would produce newsy/incident/medical/legal/tragic continuations relative to A.

Uncertainties / caveats
- Patchscope continuations were not shown here, so I can’t directly demonstrate full-sentence continuations. The diagnosis rests on the residual-norm localization plus the token-level directions from the logit lens.
- The token lists are noisy and include some unrelated tokens; the pattern is strongest in mid/late layers where the event/tragic/legal cluster repeats, which is why I emphasize that register rather than a single narrow topic.
- This could reflect a difference in a system/default prompt, a small dataset/domain training difference that affects initial-token priors, or an initialization/embedding offset at start-of-sequence — the evidence supports describing the effect (initial-token bias toward news/incident vocabulary) but not a unique causal training objective.

If you want, I can:
- run patchscope to show actual continuations produced when injecting the difference into an identity prompt, or
- show the top-ranked tokens aggregated by semantic category (news, medical, legal, neutral) to quantify the register shift.
